# Runcible

> A learning book at https://runcible.neorgon.com/. A Book is a directory of
> JSON: a manifest, chapters made of rungs, pages and exercises. The shell
> provides nine generic exercise types and knows no subject. This file is the
> Book package format, derived from tools/validate-book.mjs and
> js/exercises/spec.js, which are what decides whether a Book loads.

## Conventions that apply everywhere

- Bilingual value: a bare string, or { "en": "...", "es": "..." }. Only en and
  es exist. At least one is required where the field is required. English is
  the fallback, then Spanish. Page body and note may be arrays of paragraphs.
- No inline HTML in any content field. A "<tag>" anywhere is an error.
- Slug: lowercase, [a-z0-9-], starting with a letter or digit.
- Path: same-origin, relative to the site root, no scheme, no leading slash,
  no ".." segment. Example: "data/kana/hiragana.json".
- Data pointer: "<path>#<dotted.path>". The path must appear in the manifest's
  data[]. The fragment is a dotted lookup into the loaded JSON; a bare
  top-level key (including a non-Latin one) also resolves. Where a list is
  expected, an object resolves to its values.
- Validate with `make validate` (or `node tools/validate-book.mjs`). It exits 0
  or names the file and the field. The shell imports the same validator at
  load time, so a chapter that fails at the command line fails in the browser.

## 1. The catalog: books/index.json (neo-book-index/1)

    { "format": "neo-book-index/1",
      "books": [ { "id": "japanese", "title": { "en": "Japanese", "es": "Japones" },
                   "glyph": "あ", "state": "ready" } ] }

- format (required) "neo-book-index/1"
- books[].id (required) slug, unique, the directory name under books/
- books[].title (required) bilingual
- books[].glyph (required) one string. It is how a Book identifies itself
- books[].state (required) "ready" | "stub" | "planned". A stub opens and shows
  its ladder; a planned Book is a locked card and is never fetched

Adding a Book is one entry here plus one directory. No file under js/ changes.

## 2. The manifest: books/<id>/book.json (neo-book/1)

    { "format": "neo-book/1", "id": "piano", "version": "2026-09-04",
      "title": { "en": "Piano" }, "tagline": { "en": "..." }, "glyph": "♪",
      "lang": { "content": "en", "ui": ["en", "es"] },
      "goal": { "en": "Play a short piece to the end at a steady tempo" },
      "tracks": [], "chapters": [ ... ], "modules": [], "data": [], "credits": [] }

- format (required) "neo-book/1"
- id (required) slug equal to the directory name
- version (required) YYYY-MM-DD, bumped on any content change
- title (required), tagline, goal: bilingual
- glyph (required) one string
- accent, colour, color: FORBIDDEN. A Book may not set a colour
- lang.content (required) BCP 47 tag of what is taught; filled into every
  listen and speak exercise that does not state its own lang
- lang.ui (required) array of UI language codes
- tracks[] (optional) { id (slug), label (bilingual), description, default }.
  At most one default; with none, the first track is used
- chapters[] (required), in ladder order:
  - id (required, unique), state (required) "ready" | "stub" | "planned"
  - src: "chapters/<file>.json" relative to the Book directory. Must be null
    when state is "planned", required otherwise
  - requires: an array of chapter ids (all tracks), or an object keyed by
    track id whose keys are exactly the declared tracks. The first three
    chapters must use the array form. Every id must exist; no cycles
  - a planned chapter also carries title and note (bilingual) inline, so the
    ladder shows what is not built and why
- modules[] (optional) { path: "exercises/<file>.js" inside the Book directory,
  provides: { exercises: [...], transforms: [...] } }. provides is required
  and is exact: the module must register every id listed and nothing else
- data[] (optional, but see rule below) { src (path), licence (SPDX id or
  "public-domain"), screen "required" | "none", attribution (a credits[] id,
  required when screen is "required") }. No src twice
- credits[] { id, name }. Every attribution must name one of these

data[] is a permission list. The shell resolves a pointer, a table's items,
a figure's src or a deck's src ONLY if its path is declared here. An
undeclared path is a load error naming book.json. A data file's own _licence
block can raise the obligation (screen "required" wins over "none") and never
lower it; the validator names any disagreement.

## 3. A chapter: books/<id>/chapters/<file>.json (neo-chapter/1)

    { "format": "neo-chapter/1", "id": "1-hiragana",
      "title": { "en": "Hiragana" },
      "goal": { "statement": { "en": "Read any hiragana word aloud, with no romaji" },
                "evidence": { "skill": "kana.hiragana.read", "accuracy": 0.9,
                              "min": 40, "window": 60 } },
      "state": "ready",
      "data": ["data/kana/hiragana.json"],
      "rungs": [ { "id": "vowels", "title": { "en": "The five vowels" },
                   "unlocks": { "en": "every other row" },
                   "pages": [ ... ], "exercises": [ ... ] } ] }

- format (required) "neo-chapter/1"
- id (required) must equal the manifest entry's id
- title (required) bilingual
- goal (required) with goal.statement (required, bilingual): something the
  learner can do, never a topic name
- goal.evidence: { skill (dotted string, must contain a dot), accuracy (> 0
  and <= 1), min (positive integer), window (positive integer, >= min) }.
  THE GOAL RULE: the chapter is passed when, over the most recent `window`
  graded attempts carrying `skill`, at least `min` exist and at least
  `accuracy` of them were correct. Ungraded attempts (correct: null) do not
  enter the window. A chapter with no evidence can never be passed and cannot
  gate a later one; the validator warns
- state (optional) "ready" | "stub" | "planned"
- data[] (optional) the files to fetch when the chapter opens. Each must be
  declared in the manifest. A pointer used but not listed here warns: the file
  resolves late or not at all
- estimate, requires: accepted and not validated. Prerequisites are read from
  the manifest, not from here
- rungs[] (required): { id (required, unique), title (required), unlocks
  (bilingual, optional), pages[], exercises[] }

### Pages (rung.pages[])

Every page has id (required) and kind (required), plus optional title.

- prose: body (required; string, array, or { en: [...], es: [...] }), note,
  figure
- callout: body (required), tone (required) "note" | "warn" | "win"
- table: columns (required, array of bilingual values), and rows (array of
  arrays) or items (a data pointer to a list). With items, each column is
  matched to a field by the column string, or by column.en when the column
  is an { en, es } object
- figure: figure (required), with caption (bilingual)

figure: { kind: "svg", src (pointer), render (required string), caption } or
{ kind: "viz", builder (required), caption }. The shell draws an svg figure
only when the pointer resolves to an array of path strings, or an object
with `paths` or `s`, with a viewBox on the record, the file, or the figure.
Anything else renders a visible warning line naming what was expected
("needs path strings"); a viz figure renders "no renderer for a viz figure".
viz is not implemented.

### Exercises (rung.exercises[])

Common to every exercise: id (required, unique in the chapter), type
(required, one of the nine), skill (required, dotted string: every attempt is
recorded under it), title (bilingual, optional). Optional on any type:
count (number of items to ask; default all), pass: { accuracy } (the tick
beside the drill, never the chapter gate; forbidden on read and speak),
compare, itemIdPrefix, itemIdField, lang (BCP 47; defaults to
book.lang.content).

items is a data pointer to a list, or an inline array of objects. Field names
in the spec (prompt, answer, left, ...) name fields of those objects; dotted
paths are allowed. An answer field may hold an array: any member matches.

The nine types and their required fields (from spec.js, verbatim):

| type   | required fields                    | graded | notes |
|--------|------------------------------------|--------|-------|
| read   | pages                              | no     | whole page objects, not ids. Records correct: null per page with dwell ms |
| choice | items, prompt, answer, distractors | yes    | distractors: { n (default 3), by (a grouping field, distractors come from siblings), values (explicit list) }. `from` is ignored |
| typed  | items, prompt, answer              | yes    | transform (a Book-registered id), compare, hint: false to remove the first-letter hint |
| match  | items, left, right, n              | yes    | n pairs shown; one attempt per pairing, keyed on the left item |
| order  | items, sequence                    | yes    | sequence names a field holding an array, or a string split on whitespace; prompt optional |
| listen | items, speak, answer, respond      | yes    | respond "choice" or "typed"; speak is the field read aloud; audioOnly: true; transform allowed with respond typed |
| speak  | items, expect                      | never  | correct: null always. A transcript is shown as feedback, not a score |
| deck   | src                                | yes    | limit (positive integer), mode is review, cram or browse |
| custom | module                             | module decides | props passed through. module is an id the Book registered |

compare: pipe-separated tokens applied in order, from the closed set trim,
casefold, strip-accents, collapse-space, kana (folds katakana onto hiragana).
Default "trim|casefold". An unknown token is an error.

itemId (what stored progress is keyed by) is taken in order from: item.id
(prefixed by itemIdPrefix), the field named by itemIdField, the type's
identity field (prompt, speak, left, expect), else exercise id plus position,
which moves when the data file is edited. Give items an id.

### The deck exercise and its skill

    { "id": "e-deck-first-words", "type": "deck", "skill": "jp.vocab.read",
      "src": "books/japanese/decks/jp-first-words.json", "mode": "review",
      "limit": 20, "title": { "en": "First words, spaced" } }

src is a neo-deck/1 document (format: rappel.neorgon.com/llms.txt) on this
origin, declared in the manifest's data[]. The shell embeds Rappel in an
iframe and turns every rappel:answer into an attempt recorded under the
SPEC's skill, not the deck template's. THE SKILL RULE: a deck's skill must be
this chapter's goal.evidence.skill (the intended shape), or a skill some other
goal or non-deck exercise in the Book reads (allowed, and warned so the choice
is visible). A skill nothing in the Book reads is an error: reviews would land
nowhere with no message. A deck with no skill is an error.

### Custom exercises and transforms (modules[])

A module default-exports one function and receives a frozen object with
exactly registerExercise(id, impl), registerTransform(id, fn) and version.

    export default function register(runcible) {
      runcible.registerTransform('kana', live);          // live.settle optional
      runcible.registerExercise('jp.loanword', {
        mount(host, spec, api) { /* ... */ return { destroy() {} }; } });
    }

- an exercise id must contain a dot and its first segment must not be a
  generic type name (read, choice, typed, match, order, listen, speak, deck,
  custom). A chapter uses it as { "type": "custom", "module": "jp.loanword" }
- a transform id is any non-empty string. It runs on every keystroke of a
  typed input and may carry fn.settle(value), run once at submit before
  compare. A live half must leave an unfinished syllable alone; settle
  finishes it. The shell ships no transforms
- api is { attempt, t, tList, lang, data, tts, done }. attempt({ itemId,
  skill, correct: true|false|null, ms, answer?, expected?, hintUsed? }) is the
  only way progress is recorded. api.data(pointer) resolves a declared
  pointer. api.done(summary) ends the exercise
- a module must import nothing from js/exercises/. It may import
  js/vendor/wanakana.js and, for a Book-owned store, js/neorgon-persist.js
  (jp.lyrics does, under C8.2). Prefer a generic type; add a module only when
  none of the eight others can express the drill, and say why in a comment

### Licences

A Book never invents licensed content. It declares a data[] entry and a
pointer, and names the file a person must produce. Every file under data/
opens with a _licence block { source, url, spdx, derived, id, acknowledgement,
links, screen, generated_by, generated_at }; when screen is "required" the
acknowledgement is required and renders at the foot of every screen that
shows the file. The data/README.md in the repository is the corpus contract.
